judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver runs 'to the extent covered by property insurance obtained pursuant to this Paragraph 11.4 or other property insurance applicable to the Work,' a coverage-dependent boundary that is routinely fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Owner's property insurance amount cannot be computed because no Contract Sum is stated (5.1.1, 5.2.1, A201 9.1.1), and Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 requires a matching waiver on the Contractor's own equipment policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adjustment by the Owner 'as fiduciary' with distribution to subcontractors; the mechanism is stated, and the cross-reference to 11.4.10 is intact in the form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to subparagraphs of 11.4 that are not reproduced in the enumerated provisions here, and it presupposes Owner-purchased property insurance whose amount is indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whether discovered before or after Substantial Completion' and the inclusion of testing and Architect's costs are clear allocations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.7.3 (as revised by the Addendum) makes the cost of correcting damaged or nonconforming Work a reimbursable Cost of the Work when not caused by the Contractor's negligence, which pulls against 'costs ... shall be at the Contractor's expense.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription drops words, leaving the extension formula incomplete on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 12.2.2.1 and 9.8.4's warranty commencement; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As transcribed the sentence is missing its operative words and reads as a non-sequitur about the one-year period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the standard companion to 12.2.2.2 and consistent with 12.2.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carefully separates the correction obligation from the limitation period, but the drafting is dense and doubly negative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13.7.1 fixes deemed accrual dates and 4.6.3 bars late arbitration demands, so the interplay of correction period and limitation is spread over three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The law of the place where the Project is located' is definite here, the Project being in Hawaii.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.5.3's venue rule and Addendum 14.6(c)'s Hawaii licensing warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly transcribed but substantively the standard binding-on-successors and no-assignment-without-consent rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 13.2.2 (Owner assignment to a lender), which is not among the enumerated provisions here; otherwise consistent with 5.4.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only fragments survive in the transcription, but the substance is a standard cumulative-remedies and non-waiver clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves remedies that other provisions (4.3.10 waiver, 9.10.4-9.10.5 waivers, Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1) expressly cut back, which is a familiar tension in this form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription is fragmentary, leaving the allocation of testing responsibility hard to read from the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.4 makes laboratory fees reimbursable except those excluded by 13.5.3, so cost allocation for tests is governed jointly by the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly and, where practicable, at the normal place of testing'—a short, ordinary obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.2 and 13.5.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line requiring prompt testing to avoid delay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.2 and 13.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed-accrual rules of this kind ('any alleged cause of action shall be deemed to have accrued in any and all events not later than ...') are much litigated, and the transcription of limb .3 is partly unreadable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.6.3 measures the arbitration deadline by reference to this paragraph and 12.2.2 sets a one-year correction period, so accrual, correction and demand deadlines interlock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated stoppage grounds with a 30-day trigger; each ground is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ground .3 depends on payment 'within the time stated in the Contract Documents,' which Agreement 12.1.3 leaves blank, and Agreement 13.1 caps what the Contractor may recover on such a termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The threshold—'more than 100 percent of the total number of days scheduled for completion or 120 days in any 365-day period, whichever is less'—is awkwardly expressed and hard to apply to a contract stated as a completion date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Revised 4.3 fixes a calendar completion date rather than a number of scheduled days, so the first limb of the formula has no clear input.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Persistently failed to fulfill the Owner's obligations ... with respect to matters important to the progress of the Work' is evaluative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recovery is 'as provided in Subparagraph 14.1.3,' which Agreement 13.1 caps at the for-cause measure in 13.2 with a modified fee calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific grounds followed by 'otherwise is guilty of substantial breach of a provision of the Contract Documents'—a catch-all against enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.2 governs the payment consequences of a for-cause termination, and Addendum 6.5 gives the Owner a separate discretionary termination right if the Preliminary Budget is unacceptable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires Architect certification and seven days' notice, then lists three permitted actions; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 conditions termination payments on the Contractor executing assignments and 5.4.1 makes the assignment contingent, so three provisions govern the same step.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The computation is clear arithmetic once 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum' is known.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Contract Sum is stated (5.1.1 defines it as Cost of the Work plus Fee and 5.2.1's maximum is 'N/A'), and Agreement 13.2 imposes a different cap and calculation for the same termination; the two measures cannot both control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare suspension right 'for such period of time as the Owner may determine'; broad but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.4 directs that on suspension 'the Guaranteed Maximum Price and Contract Time shall be increased,' but there is no Guaranteed Maximum Price to increase.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line convenience-termination right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 substantially limits the payment consequences of exercising it, so the right and its price are stated in different documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated duties on receipt of notice; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.4.1 and Agreement 13.3 on subcontract assignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed' is a compensation measure with no stated basis for computing profit on unperformed work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.1 expressly provides that the amount payable under this subparagraph 'shall not exceed' the for-cause measure in 13.2, with the Fee calculated as if the Work were completed, and 4.3.10 waives loss of profit except anticipated profit arising directly from the Work—two contrary measures for the same payment.
